[[Air Chief Marshal]] '''Sir Brian Kevin Burridge''',<ref name="commission"/> (born 26 September 1949) is a retired [[Royal Air Force]] officer. A former [[Hawker Siddeley Nimrod|Nimrod]] pilot, Burridge was in overall command of British forces under [[Operation Telic]] during the [[2003 invasion of Iraq]].

==RAF career==
Brian Burridge joined the [[Royal Air Force]] as a university cadet (as a member of [[Cambridge University Air Squadron]]), being commissioned on 24 September 1967.<ref name="commission">{{London Gazette|issue=44449|supp=y|page=12344|date=14 November 1967}}</ref> He was a pilot with an operational background in the maritime patrol role, serving on Nos [[No. 206 Squadron RAF|206]] and [[No. 120 Squadron RAF|120]] Squadrons.

Burridge was promoted to the rank of [[Pilot Officer]] on 15 July 1970,<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=45191|supp=y|page=10106|date=15 September 1970}}</ref> to [[Flying Officer]] on 15 January 1971,<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=45283|supp=y|page=674|date=19 January 1971}}</ref> [[Flight Lieutenant]] on 13 April 1972<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=45648|supp=y|page=4586|date=13 April 1972}}</ref> to [[Squadron Leader]] on 1 July 1979<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=47911|supp=y|pages=9361–9362|date=24 July 1979}}</ref> and to [[Wing Commander (rank)|Wing Commander]] on 1 July 1985.<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=50195|supp=y|page=9770|date=16 July 1985}}</ref> In 1986 he attended the [[Royal Naval College, Greenwich|Royal Naval Staff College]] and then later that year went on to command [[No. 236 Operational Conversion Unit RAF]]. Promoted to [[Group Captain]] in 1990,<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=52200|supp=y|page=11367|date=3 July 1990}}</ref> he became officer commanding [[RAF Kinloss]].

From 1992 Burridge served in the [[Ministry of Defence (United Kingdom)|Ministry of Defence]], initially as Deputy Director of Force Doctrine (RAF) and later becoming the Director of Force Development in the Central Staff before being made Principal Staff Officer to the [[Chief of the Defence Staff (United Kingdom)|Chief of the Defence Staff]] in 1994 in the rank of [[Air Commodore]].<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=53537|supp=y|page=20689|date=4 January 1994}}</ref> In 1997 he attended the Cabinet Office Top Management Programme and then later in the year became a Defence Fellow at [[King's College London]]. In 1998 he attended the Higher Command and Staff Course being promoted to [[Air Vice Marshal]] on 1 July 1998.<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=55220|supp=y|page=8727|date=11 August 1998}}</ref> He then served as Air Officer Commanding [[No. 11/18 Group RAF]]. In January 2000 he became Commandant of the [[Joint Services Command and Staff College]], subsequently moving the college into a Public Private Partnership at [[Shrivenham]]. On 12 February 2002, Burridge was promoted to [[air marshal]] and appointed Deputy [[Commander-in-Chief]], [[RAF Strike Command|Strike Command]].<ref name="AM">{{London Gazette|issue=56478|supp=y|page=1765|date=12 February 2002}}</ref>

Burridge was in overall command of British forces under [[Operation Telic]] during the [[2003 invasion of Iraq]].<ref name="profile">{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/3009897.stm|title=Profile: Air Marshal Sir Brian Burridge|date=8 May 2003|work=[[BBC News]]|publisher=[[BBC]]|access-date=26 February 2010}}</ref> In June 2003, Burridge appeared before the [[House of Commons of the United Kingdom|Commons]] [[Defence Select Committee]], telling MPs of delays in distributing equipment to troops in Iraq and of his role in vetoing potentially controversial air strikes while he was in command in Iraq.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/politics/2982892.stm|title=Boots too late for UK troops|date=11 June 2003|work=[[BBC News]]|publisher=[[BBC]]|access-date=1 March 2010}}</ref> He was appointed a [[Knight Commander of the Order of the Bath]] "for gallant and distinguished services whilst on operations in Iraq during the period 19 March to 19 April 2003" on 31 October 2003.<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=57100|supp=y|page=2|date=31 October 2003}}</ref>

In July 2003 Burridge became Commander-in-Chief [[RAF Strike Command]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rafweb.org/Cmd_H4.htm|title=RAF Commands|publisher=Air of Authority|accessdate=1 April 2014|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140705160727/http://www.rafweb.org/Cmd_H4.htm|archivedate=5 July 2014}}</ref> He served as [[air Aide-de-Camp]] to [[Queen Elizabeth II]] from 31 July 2003 to 17 January 2006.<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=57018|supp=y|page=9733|date=5 August 2003}}</ref><ref>{{London Gazette|issue=57875|supp=y|page=630|date=17 January 2006}}</ref> He retired on 18 January 2006 with the rank of [[Air Chief Marshal]],<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=57906|supp=y|page=2497|date=21 February 2006}}</ref> though his commission in the reserve was extended to January 2015.<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=59341|supp=y|page=3089|date=23 February 2010}}</ref>

On 8 December 2009, Burridge [[List of witnesses of The Iraq Inquiry#December 8|gave evidence]] to [[The Iraq Inquiry]].<ref name="BBC XIV">{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/uk_politics/8402313.stm|title=UK military chief told 'when not if' over Iraq invasion|date=8 December 2009|work=[[BBC News]]|publisher=[[BBC]]|access-date=28 January 2010}}</ref>

On 1 October 2018, Burridge became [[chief executive officer]] of the [[Royal Aeronautical Society]].<ref name=ceraes>{{cite web |title=Royal Aeronautical Society announces new CEO |url=https://www.aerosociety.com/news/royal-aeronautical-society-announces-new-ceo/ |publisher=RAeS |access-date=23 April 2019 |archive-date=23 April 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190423070014/https://www.aerosociety.com/news/royal-aeronautical-society-announces-new-ceo/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Interests==
In 2005 Air Marshal Burridge was president of the RAF Mountaineering Association and a trustee of the Windsor Leadership Trust. Burridge sat as chair of the [[Bentley Priory]] Battle of Britain Trust and was present at the facility's closing ceremony in 2007.<ref name="priory">{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/6907537.stm|title=Sad salute to war command centre|last=McClatchey|first=Caroline|date=20 July 2007|work=[[BBC News]]|publisher=[[BBC]]|access-date=28 February 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.harrowtimes.co.uk/news/4438437.Picnic_concert_at_RAF_Bentley_Priory/|title=Picnic concert at RAF Bentley Priory|last=Royston|first=Jack|date=15 June 2009|work=Harrow Times|publisher=[[Newsquest]]|accessdate=1 March 2010}}</ref> He attained a [[master's degree]] in business administration from the [[Open University]].<ref>[http://www8.open.ac.uk/business-school/news/archive/military-leader-and-mba-graduate-pays-tribute-ou-business-school?samsredir=1301546053 Military leader and MBA graduate pays tribute to the OU Business School]</ref>
